To find the determinant of the 4x4 matrix, I will expand it along the first row. The matrix is:
$$
\left(
\begin{array}{cccc}
 -3 & -4 & -2 & 3 \\
 0 & 4 & -4 & -2 \\
 3 & -3 & 4 & -2 \\
 4 & 2 & -2 & -1 \\
\end{array}
\right)
$$
The formula for the determinant expansion along the first row is:
$|A| = a_{11}C_{11} + a_{12}C_{12} + a_{13}C_{13} + a_{14}C_{14}$
where $C_{1j} = (-1)^{1+j} |M_{1j}|$.

Let's calculate the determinant of each corresponding 3x3 minor matrix:

1. For $C_{11}$, the minor matrix is obtained by removing the first row and first column:
$|M_{11}| = \left|
\begin{array}{ccc}
 4 & -4 & -2 \\
 -3 & 4 & -2 \\
 2 & -2 & -1 \\
\end{array}
\right| = 4(-4 - 4) - (-4)(3 - (-4)) - 2(6 - 8) = 4(-8) + 4(7) - 2(-2) = -32 + 28 + 4 = 0$

2. For $C_{12}$, the minor matrix is obtained by removing the first row and second column:
$|M_{12}| = \left|
\begin{array}{ccc}
 0 & -4 & -2 \\
 3 & 4 & -2 \\
 4 & -2 & -1 \\
\end{array}
\right| = 0 - (-4)(-3 - (-8)) - 2(-6 - 16) = 4(-5) - 2(-22) = -20 + 44 = 24$

3. For $C_{13}$, the minor matrix is obtained by removing the first row and third column:
$|M_{13}| = \left|
\begin{array}{ccc}
 0 & 4 & -2 \\
 3 & -3 & -2 \\
 4 & 2 & -1 \\
\end{array}
\right| = 0 - 4(-3 - (-8)) - 2(6 - (-12)) = -4(5) - 2(18) = -20 - 36 = -56$

4. For $C_{14}$, the minor matrix is obtained by removing the first row and fourth column:
$|M_{14}| = \left|
\begin{array}{ccc}
 0 & 4 & -4 \\
 3 & -3 & 4 \\
 4 & 2 & -2 \\
\end{array}
\right| = 0 - 4(-6 - 16) - 4(6 - (-12)) = -4(-22) - 4(18) = 88 - 72 = 16$

Now, substitute the minors back into the determinant formula with their respective signs:
$|A| = -3(0) - (-4)(24) + (-2)(-56) - 3(16)$
$|A| = 0 + 96 + 112 - 48 = 160$

The determinant of the matrix is 160.
